name: Peter

seo.title: Saint Peter the Apostle: his life, the rock and how he died
seo.description: Peter in plain words: the fisherman Jesus called the rock, his denial and return, how he died in Rome, his feast days, and the myths.

band.lede: The fisherman Jesus called the rock. He denied Him three times, was forgiven, and led the Church.

Behind him are a rock hung with ivy and a stormy blue sky. In the distance, lower left, a small scene of the empty tomb.

who: Peter was a fisherman from Galilee named Simon. Jesus gave him a new name, Cephas, the rock. He is first in every list of the Twelve, and often spoke for them. On the night Jesus was arrested, he denied Him three times. Forgiven, he led the first Christians in Jerusalem. He died a martyr at Rome under Nero.

tidbits.text: Jesus gave him his new name. **Cephas** is the Aramaic word for rock, and **Peter** is the same name in Greek.
He is named first in every list of the Twelve. Matthew says it outright: “first Simon, called Peter”.
The New Testament mentions a charcoal fire only twice. Peter stood by one when he denied Jesus. By the other, on the shore, Jesus asked him three times, “Do you love Me?”

cite.text: John 18:18 and 21:9; Strong's Greek 439, at Bible Hub

tidbits.text: A letter under his name admits that some parts of Paul's letters “are hard to understand”.

A fishhook appears just once in the New Testament. When collectors of the temple tax came to Peter, Jesus sent him to the sea with a hook. In the mouth of the first fish he caught, he would find a four-drachma coin: “Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.”

cite.text: Matthew 17:24-27; Strong's Greek 44, at Bible Hub

facts.label: Born
facts.text: In Galilee, in a year no one recorded. John's Gospel says he came from **Bethsaida**, the town of Andrew and Philip.

facts.label: Home
facts.text: **Capernaum**, on the Sea of Galilee. He shared a house there with his brother Andrew.

facts.label: Family
facts.text: His father was John, or Jonah. His brother **Andrew** was an apostle too. He was **married**: Jesus healed his mother-in-law, and Paul says his wife travelled with him. Clement of Alexandria says he had children.

facts.label: Work
facts.text: A **fisherman**, in partnership with James and John, the sons of Zebedee.

facts.label: Also called
facts.text: **Simon**, his own name. **Cephas**, the Aramaic form of his new name. **Simon Peter**. The **Leader of the Apostles**, in the Orthodox Church. The **Prince of the Apostles**, in Catholic writing.

facts.label: Died
facts.text: At **Rome**, under the emperor **Nero**, in the 60s. Tertullian and Origen say he was crucified. Jerome puts it in Nero's last year.

facts.label: Buried
facts.text: On the **Vatican Hill**, says Jerome. About 200, Gaius of Rome already pointed visitors there, to the apostles' memorials. Constantine built a church over the grave, and today's **St Peter's** replaced it.

facts.label: Wrote
facts.text: Two letters bear his name, **1 Peter** and **2 Peter**. Eusebius counts the first as undisputed. He had learned that the second was not in the canon, though many used it. Jerome says many doubted it for its style. Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant Bibles all have both. Some scholars today doubt he wrote them, says *Britannica*.

facts.label: Patron of
facts.text: **Fishermen**, **Rome** and **popes**, says *Britannica*. Locksmiths too, for the keys.

facts.label: In art
facts.text: Holding **keys**, for “the keys of the kingdom of heaven”. The oldest pictures give him a strong, round head, with **thick curly hair and a beard**. Keys became his sign from the end of the 500s.

portrait.alt: A worn icon on wood: Peter, grey-haired with a short grey beard, gazes straight out before a gold halo. He wears a white cloak, holds keys in his right hand, and carries a cross on a long staff over his shoulder.
portrait.credit: Saint Peter, an encaustic icon of the 500s or 600s. St Catherine's Monastery, Mount Sinai. Public domain.
portrait.caption: An icon painted in hot wax in the 500s or 600s, kept at St Catherine's Monastery on Mount Sinai. He holds the keys, and a cross on a long staff. Public domain.

typeNote: The test names him for one night. “Even if all fall away on account of You, I never will,” he said. That same night he denied Christ three times. Then he wept, came back, and led the Church.

west.text: The **Confession of Peter**, for the **Episcopal Church** and Lutherans in the **Missouri Synod** and the **ELCA**. Until 1960 Rome kept his **Chair at Rome** on this day.
The **Chair of Peter**, a **Catholic** feast. Until 1960 this was his **Chair at Antioch**.

**Peter and Paul**, a **Catholic** solemnity. Also the **Episcopal Church**, and Lutherans in the **Missouri Synod** and the **ELCA**. The **Church of England** keeps it too, and may keep Peter alone.
**St Peter in Chains**, in the **1916 Roman Martyrology**: the day his church on the Esquiline in Rome was dedicated. Dropped from Rome's calendar in 1960.
The **dedication of the basilicas** of Peter and Paul in Rome. A **Catholic** optional memorial.

east.text: The **chains of Peter**, honoured by the **OCA** and the **Greek** churches. The **Russian Church** keeps the day on the old calendar, which is 29 January on today's.
**Peter and Paul**, the leaders of the apostles, for the **OCA** and the **Greek** churches.
All **twelve apostles** together, the next day, in the **OCA**.
The **Coptic** Church, on 5 Abib in its own calendar: the martyrdom of Peter and Paul. The **Russian Church**'s 29 June falls on this day too.

feasts.note: Why 29 June? A Roman list of martyrs' days, made in 354, keeps Peter and Paul on this day and dates the feast from 258. The same list has his Chair on 22 February. Rome's reform of 1960 dropped 18 January and 1 August as repeats, so the 1962 Missal keeps 22 February, 29 June and 18 November. The Week of Prayer for Christian Unity runs from the Confession of Peter on 18 January to the Conversion of Paul on 25 January. Churches on the old calendar keep each date 13 days later.

said.lede: Jesus, Paul and the first generations after them, in their own words.

quotes.q: Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.
quotes.who: Jesus, when Peter called Him the Christ

quotes.q: Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift all of you like wheat. But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.
quotes.who: Jesus, at the Last Supper, hours before Peter denied Him

quotes.q: James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship.
quotes.who: Paul, on his visit to the apostles in Jerusalem

quotes.who: Ignatius of Antioch, writing to the Christians of Rome, on his way to die there

moments.title: The catch of fish
moments.text: Jesus taught the crowd from Simon's boat. Then He told him to put out into deep water and let down the nets. Simon had worked all night and caught nothing. “But because You say so, I will let down the nets.” The nets began to tear, and both boats began to sink. Simon fell at Jesus' knees. “Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.” Jesus said to him, “Do not be afraid. From now on you will catch men.” They left everything and followed Him.

moments.when: The fourth watch of the night
moments.title: Walking on the water
moments.text: The disciples' boat was far from land, with the wind against it. Jesus came to them, walking on the sea. Peter called out, “Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the water.” Jesus said, “Come.” Peter got down out of the boat and walked on the water toward Him. But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid and began to sink. “Lord, save me!” Jesus reached out His hand at once. “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”

moments.title: “Who do you say I am?”
moments.text: Jesus asked the disciples, “But what about you? Who do you say I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus called him blessed, and said, “you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church.” What He meant has been argued over ever since: see The rock, below. Then Jesus began to tell them He must suffer and be killed. Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him. “Far be it from You, Lord! This shall never happen to You!” Jesus turned and said, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me.”

moments.title: The Transfiguration
moments.text: Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain. There His face shone like the sun, and Moses and Elijah appeared, talking with Him. Peter spoke up: “Lord, it is good for us to be here.” He offered to put up three shelters. Mark says they were all so terrified “that Peter did not know what else to say.” Then a voice from a bright cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!” The second letter under Peter's name remembers the day: “we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.”

moments.title: The foot-washing
moments.text: Jesus got up from supper, wrapped a towel around His waist, and began to wash the disciples' feet. When He came to Peter, Peter said, “Never shall You wash my feet!” Jesus answered, “Unless I wash you, you have no part with Me.” So Peter asked for more: “not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!”

moments.title: The sword
moments.text: Judas came to the garden with soldiers and officers, carrying torches and weapons. Simon Peter drew his sword and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus. Jesus said to Peter, “Put your sword back in its sheath! Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given Me?” Luke adds that Jesus touched the man's ear and healed him.

moments.title: Three denials, and a look
moments.text: Peter followed at a distance and sat by the fire in the courtyard. A servant girl looked hard at him. “This man also was with Him.” Peter said, “Woman, I do not know Him.” Twice more someone said it, and twice more he denied it. While he was still speaking, the rooster crowed. “And the Lord turned and looked at Peter.” Peter remembered what Jesus had told him, “and he went outside and wept bitterly.”

moments.when: The first day of the week
moments.title: The race to the tomb
moments.text: Mary Magdalene ran to tell Peter and the other disciple that the Lord had been taken from the tomb. The two ran there together. The other disciple outran Peter and got there first, but did not go in. Peter came just after him and went in, and saw the linen cloths lying there. Later that day the disciples were saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!” Paul's list of those who saw the risen Lord begins with him: “He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.”

moments.title: Breakfast on the shore
moments.text: Peter said, “I am going fishing,” and six others went with him. They caught nothing all night. Early in the morning, a man on the shore told them to cast the net on the right side, and it filled. When the disciple Jesus loved said, “It is the Lord!”, Peter put on his outer garment and jumped into the sea. After breakfast by a charcoal fire, Jesus asked him three times, “Do you love Me?” The third time, Peter was deeply hurt. “Lord, You know all things. You know I love You.” Each time Jesus gave him a charge: “Feed My lambs.” “Shepherd My sheep.” “Feed My sheep.”

moments.title: The first sermon
moments.text: When the day of Pentecost came, the disciples were filled with the Holy Spirit, and a crowd gathered. Peter stood up with the Eleven and spoke. He told them God had raised Jesus, Whom they had crucified. They were cut to the heart. “Brothers, what shall we do?” Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins.” About three thousand were baptised that day.

moments.title: Before the Council
moments.text: After a lame man was healed at the temple, Peter and John were arrested. Filled with the Holy Spirit, Peter told the rulers, “Salvation exists in no one else.” They saw the boldness of these “unschooled, ordinary men”, and took note “that these men had been with Jesus.” Ordered never to teach in the name of Jesus, Peter and John answered, “we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

moments.title: Cornelius
moments.text: At Joppa, Peter went up on a roof to pray and saw a vision: a great sheet full of animals, and a voice. “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!” He refused. “I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.” The voice answered, “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.” Then men came from Cornelius, a centurion at Caesarea. When Cornelius fell at his feet, Peter helped him up. “I am only a man myself.” As Peter preached to the people gathered in his house, the Holy Spirit fell on these Gentiles, and Peter had them baptised.

moments.title: The angel and the chains
moments.text: King Herod had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword. Then he arrested Peter. The night before his trial, Peter was asleep between two soldiers, bound with two chains. An angel woke him, and the chains fell off his wrists. An iron gate opened by itself. Peter thought he was seeing a vision. He went to the house of Mary, the mother of Mark, where many were praying. A servant girl named Rhoda knew his voice. She was so overjoyed “that she forgot to open the gate.”

moments.title: Saved by grace
moments.text: Some believers taught that Gentile Christians must be circumcised and obey the law of Moses. The apostles and elders met. After much discussion, Peter reminded them how God had given the Holy Spirit to the Gentiles. Why put on them “a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear”? “We believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.”

moments.title: Paul opposes him
moments.text: At Antioch, Peter used to eat with Gentile believers. When certain men came from James, he drew back, for fear of the circumcision group. Other Jewish believers followed him, even Barnabas. Paul writes, “I opposed him to his face.” In front of them all he asked, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?” The second letter under Peter's name calls Paul “our beloved brother”.

miracles.lede: Acts tells of wonders done through Peter. He was quick to say where the power came from:

pledge.q: Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk?

items.title: The man lame from birth
items.text: A man lame from birth was carried to the temple gate every day to beg. He asked Peter and John for money. Peter told him to look at them, and spoke in the name of Jesus. He took him by the right hand and helped him up. At once the man's feet and ankles were made strong.
items.quote: walking and leaping and praising God
items.witness: All the people knew him as the beggar from the gate. Acts adds that he was over forty years old.

items.title: His shadow
items.text: The apostles did many signs and wonders. People carried the sick into the streets on cots and mats, so that Peter's shadow might fall on some of them as he passed. Crowds came from the towns around Jerusalem too, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits.
items.quote: and all of them were healed

items.title: Aeneas
items.text: At Lydda, Peter found a man named Aeneas. He had been paralysed and bedridden for eight years. Peter spoke to him, and he got up at once.
items.quote: Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and put away your mat.
items.witness: All who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, says Acts, and turned to the Lord.

items.title: Tabitha raised
items.text: At Joppa lived a disciple named Tabitha, always busy with works of kindness. She fell sick and died. The widows stood around Peter, weeping, and showed him the clothes she had made. He sent them all out of the room. He knelt down and prayed, and turned toward her body.
items.witness: She opened her eyes and sat up. He presented her alive to the saints and widows, and it became known all over Joppa.

more.title: Ananias and Sapphira
more.text: A couple sold a piece of land and kept back part of the money, while pretending to give it all. Peter told Ananias he had lied to the Holy Spirit, and Ananias fell down and died. About three hours later his wife told the same lie, and died too. “And great fear came over the whole church.”
more.quote: You have not lied to men, but to God!

more.title: The open prison
more.text: The high priest had the apostles put in the public jail. During the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors and brought them out. At daybreak they were back in the temple courts, teaching. The officers sent to fetch them came back with a strange report.
more.quote: We found the jail securely locked, with the guards posted at the doors; but when we opened them, we found no one inside.

words.note: Two letters in the Bible bear his name, and Acts records his sermons. Outside the quiz's own section, every Bible line on this page is from the Berean Standard Bible.

feature.q: Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life. We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God.
feature.ctx: Many disciples had stopped following Jesus. He asked the Twelve, “Do you want to leave too?” Peter answered for them.

quotes.q: Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!
quotes.who: To a man lame from birth, begging at the temple gate.

quotes.q: We must obey God rather than men.
quotes.who: Peter and the apostles, to the high priest, who had ordered them to stop teaching in Jesus' name.

quotes.q: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect.
quotes.who: From his first letter, to Christians living as exiles.

quotes.q: Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.
quotes.who: From his first letter, just before he warns that the devil prowls “like a roaring lion”.

quotes.q: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.
quotes.who: From the second letter under his name. It answers those who scoffed, “Where is the promise of His coming?”

myths.claim: He asked to be crucified upside down, because he felt unworthy to die as Jesus did.
myths.truth: The Bible does not say how he was crucified. Origen, as Eusebius quotes him, says Peter was “crucified head-downwards; for he had requested that he might suffer in this way”. He gives no reason. The *Acts of Peter* has the same detail, with a mystical reason of its own. It is a story written by about 200, and never part of the Bible. The humble reason appears in Jerome, in 392: Peter said “he was unworthy to be crucified in the same manner as his Lord.”

cite.text: John 21:18-19; Origen, in Eusebius, Church History, Book 3, chapter 1; Acts of Peter, chapters 37 and 38, tr. M. R. James (1924); Jerome, Lives of Illustrious Men, chapter 1

myths.claim: “Quo vadis?” Leaving Rome, Peter met Jesus and asked Him where He was going.
myths.truth: Not in the Bible. The story comes from the *Acts of Peter*. There Jesus answers, “I go into Rome to be crucified,” and Peter turns back to die. Ambrose, bishop of Milan, told it again in a sermon. The Bible does have Peter ask, “Lord, where are You going?”, but at the Last Supper. In the Latin Bible those words are {la|Domine, quo vadis?}

cite.text: Acts of Peter, chapter 35, tr. M. R. James (1924); Ambrose, Sermon against Auxentius; John 13:36, in the Vulgate

myths.claim: Peter stands at the pearly gates and decides who gets into heaven.
myths.truth: Not in Scripture. Jesus promised him “the keys of the kingdom of heaven”, and *Britannica* says that is why art puts him at heaven's gates. But the gates of pearl belong to the new Jerusalem in Revelation. There each gate is a single pearl, and the Bible puts “twelve angels at the gates”.
Peter denied Jesus three times. In Mark, the rooster crows twice: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” Matthew, Luke and John tell of it crowing once.

The New Testament never says he did. His first letter sends greetings from “The church in Babylon”, and early writers took Babylon to mean Rome. The next generations tie him to Rome, and to his death there. Ignatius was a bishop taken to Rome to die. He tells the Romans he does not command them “as Peter and Paul” did. Dionysius, bishop of Corinth, says the two “taught together in like manner in Italy, and suffered martyrdom at the same time.” About 200, Gaius of Rome could show the apostles' memorials on the Vatican Hill and the Ostian Way.

cite.text: 1 Peter 5:13; Eusebius, Church History, Book 2, chapters 15 and 25; Ignatius, Letter to the Romans, chapter 4

myths.claim: The Bible calls Peter the first pope.
myths.truth: The word pope is not in the Bible. The New Testament never places Peter at the head of the church in Rome. The early writers count Rome's bishops from the apostles, in different ways. Irenaeus says Peter and Paul founded the church there, and “committed into the hands of Linus the office of the episcopate”. Eusebius calls Linus “Peter's successor in the episcopate”. Jerome says Peter himself “held the sacerdotal chair there for twenty-five years”. The Catholic Church counts Peter as the first pope. Whether his place passed to Rome's bishops is the question of The rock, below.

cite.text: Irenaeus, Against Heresies, Book 3, chapter 3; Eusebius, Church History, Book 3, chapters 2 and 4; Jerome, Lives of Illustrious Men, chapter 1; Britannica

extras.title: The rock
extras.lede: Jesus said to him, “you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church” (Matthew 16:18). Christians have long disagreed about what the rock is, and what it meant for the Church after Peter. Here each side speaks for itself.

items.title: The Catholic reading
items.text: The rock is Peter. The *Catholic Encyclopedia* notes that in Aramaic one word, Kipha, means both Peter and rock. In 1870 the First Vatican Council taught that Christ gave Peter a true primacy of jurisdiction over the whole Church: a first place with real authority. It pointed to the keys he was promised, and to “Feed My sheep.” It taught too that this primacy lives on in his successors, the bishops of Rome.
items.quote: We therefore teach and declare that, according to the testimony of the Gospel, the primacy of jurisdiction over the universal Church of God was immediately and directly promised and given to blessed Peter the Apostle by Christ the Lord.

cite.text: First Vatican Council, Pastor Aeternus, chapters 1 and 2, in Philip Schaff's The Creeds of Christendom; Catholic Encyclopedia, “St. Peter”

items.title: The Orthodox reading
items.text: The rock is the faith Peter confessed. A sermon of Augustine says so, and the OCA gives it as its reading for 29 June. The Orthodox honour Peter as the foremost of the apostles. But the *Longer Catechism* of Philaret of Moscow names Christ as the Church's only Head. The Russian Church's Holy Synod approved it. Asked what authority reaches over the whole Church, the catechism answers, “An œcumenical Council.” John Chrysostom read the rock this way:
items.quote: upon this rock will I build My Church; that is, on the faith of his confession.

cite.text: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 54; the OCA, 29 June; the Longer Catechism, questions 259 and 278, tr. R. W. Blackmore

items.title: The Protestant reading
items.text: The rock is the confession of Christ, the Church's only foundation. Some later Protestant scholars read it as Peter himself, like the Lutheran Oscar Cullmann. But he held that Peter began no line of successors. John Calvin gave Peter first place among the apostles, but not power over them: “Let Peter have the preeminence, still there is a great difference between the honour of rank and the possession of power.” On the rock itself he wrote:
items.quote: Peter had confessed in his own name, and that of his brethren, that Christ was the Son of God. On this rock Christ builds His Church, because it is the only foundation.

cite.text: John Calvin, Institutes of the Christian Religion, Book 4, chapter 6, tr. Henry Beveridge (1845); Wikipedia, “Saint Peter”, on Oscar Cullmann

items.title: Augustine left it open
items.text: Augustine gave both readings in his life. As a priest, he wrote that the Church was founded on Peter as on a rock. Many people sang the same thought, he says, in a hymn of Ambrose about the rooster's crow. Later he often explained the rock as Christ, Whom Peter confessed. Looking back over his books in his *Retractations*, he did not choose. Our translation:
items.quote: Of these two opinions, let the reader choose which is the more probable.

cite.text: Augustine, Retractations, Book 1, chapter 21, from the Latin

death.big: He died at Rome under the emperor Nero, in the 60s. The early writers say he was crucified.
paras: Jesus had told him how it would end. “When you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go.” John adds that He said this “to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God.”
The second letter under his name knows the end is near: “this tent will soon be laid aside, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.”
About 97, Clement of Rome wrote that “the greatest and most righteous pillars [of the Church]” had been put to death through envy. He named Peter first, then Paul.

Tertullian takes up Jesus' words: “At Rome Nero was the first who stained with blood the rising faith. Then is Peter girt by another, when he is made fast to the cross.” Lactantius says the same of Nero: “he crucified Peter, and slew Paul”.

About 200, a Roman named Gaius told a rival teacher, “if you will go to the Vatican or to the Ostian way, you will find the trophies of those who laid the foundations of this church.” Eusebius took these trophies to mark the apostles' graves. Jerome says Peter was “buried at Rome in the Vatican near the triumphal way”. Constantine built a church over the grave, and today's St Peter's stands in its place.

later.title: A story Clement heard
later.text: Clement of Alexandria passes on a story. Peter saw his own wife led out to die. He “rejoiced because of her summons and her return home”, and called to her by name: “Oh thou, remember the Lord.”

cite.text: Clement of Alexandria, Stromata, Book 7, in Eusebius, Church History, Book 3, chapter 30

saint.big: Yes. Every church that keeps saints' days honours him, and most keep his day with Paul's, on 29 June.

churches.note: A Festival in the Church of England
Missouri Synod and ELCA, 18 January and 29 June

paras: The Orthodox call Peter and Paul the leaders of the apostles, the *koryphaioi*. In Greek drama the word meant the leaders of the chorus.

Was he the first pope? The Catholic Church counts him so. It teaches that his primacy over the whole Church lives on in the bishops of Rome. The Orthodox and Protestants honour him as first among the apostles, but do not accept that teaching. Each side's own words are in The rock, above.
Rome's book of martyrs, in its 1916 edition, gives his day like this:

quotes.q: At Rome, the birthday of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, who suffered martyrdom on the same day, under the emperor Nero.

reads.title: The Gospel of Mark
reads.text: The shortest Gospel, in sixteen chapters. Papias, an early bishop, says Mark was Peter's interpreter. He wrote down what he remembered “of the things said or done by Christ”.
